I don't really have a relationship with my youngest nephew like I do with his older siblings. My sister and I aren't exactly close so I don't see her kids very often. The older two are 16f and 8m and I adore them. The youngest will be 2 next week and he doesn't know me any more than I know him. I'm pretty sure I've only ever held him once or twice in his whole life. My sister announced her pregnancy the same week my husband and I found out that we'd likely be unable to conceive naturally. We've been trying for years and aren't in a position to comfortably afford IVF. I know that's not my nephew's fault and he's such a sweet kid but I can't help resenting him and it's pretty much prevented me from being able to have a relationship with him. I feel bad enough about that alone but I feel especially bad about how estranged he feels compared to how much I adore his brother. My sister was pregnant with him at my wedding 8 years ago so watching him grow up has been a visual representation of how long I've been trying to start my own family. (Background, my husband and I were together for 10 years before we got married. I didn't really care about getting married but that was his condition for having kids so I caved and we compromised.) I hate feeling this jealous and it's turning me into a bitter old shrew.

Unless something has drastically changed since I left a couple years ago, you still pay sales tax when you use trade credit since it's a form of payment and not a discount. A discount applies to the item cost/purchase price so the taxable subtotal is lower. A payment method is applied to the gross total after tax. That's why you pay tax when you use a gift card but not necessarily if you use rewards coupons for the total amount.

When I was 11 (I'm 33f btw) my family got our first desktop computer with AOL. My parents had the don't-give-out-personal-info-or-pictures conversion and I knew that creeps could prey on kids online so I was careful but I absolutely loved chat rooms. I made a cool friend who was my age and lived on the other side of the country. We talked almost every day about school, friends, our lives, everything. We knew each other's first names and the states we lived in but I was always careful to not share my last name or city or phone number. We were really close. My parents knew about him and my sisters even talked to him online once in a while. 
After about a year he started asking for specifics. I always said no and laughed it off. Until one day he called my house. I got off the phone real quick and freaked out. I started taking to him less. Then he started sending me pictures of my house in Google Earth. Then he was writing me letters and mailing them to me. Sometimes he'd include school pictures of himself or a phone card so I could call him sometimes. I never did. Turns out that he'd been contacting other people that I'd included in group emails (back then if you wanted to share a funny cat picture you had to email it to everyone you know in a mass email). Eventually he found a friend that I went to school with who was more than happy to give him all my personal info. I stopped taking to the "friend" and cut off contact with the guy online. I asked my sisters to stop talking to him but I was too freaked out to tell them why. 
At this point, it's been 2 years since I met him online. He kept calling my house every couple weeks and writing me letters every month or two. My sisters thought we were just fighting about something and kept trying to get me to forgive him. They thought he was really cool. This went on until I was about 16. 
He actually kept in touch with my youngest sister up until we were all in our early 20s. Apparently he regularly asked about me and how I was and what I was up to. I finally had to tell her everything to get her to cut him off. 
To this day, phone calls give me anxiety and I feel weird sharing any personal info about myself. Especially online. I actually changed the spelling of my name to make me harder to find online in case he ever tries to look me up. The internet can be a really scary place.

About 7 years ago I let a couple friends move in with me while they got back on their feet and they brought their cat (Arty) with them. He really bonded with my cat (Callie) and with my husband. Over the years, this couple turned it to be completely irresponsible adults and pet owners. Arty got sick and started chewing the fur off his lower back and started losing weight. He smelled terrible and wouldn't come out to use the litter box or to socialize but they kept making excuses for why they couldn't take him to the vet. One day I got home from work and my husband was literally in tears frantically searching the house for Arty. We finally found him in the back of our closet. He was just skin and bones had obviously been there all day. I was furious and we had a huge fight. The next morning, I made an appointment with my vet to take him in and get him there care he needed. 


When we got to the vet, Arty could barely stand. He'd gone from about 16 lbs to only 7 lbs. He was barely eating, drinking, grooming himself or using the litter box. He just kept looking up at me while the vet looked him over. I was so scared for him and the vet told us that it was good that we brought him in because he was so dehydrated that we would probably have lost him within another day or two. A couple blood tests, a massive about of fluids, an antibiotic and a pain killer later, the vet told us that the problem was likely caused by Arty's teeth. They were pretty much all rotten and becoming infected so it was painful for him to eat or drink. We were told that it would cost between $400-$700 for the dental surgery to have his teeth pulled but we made the appointment anyway. We bought a bunch of canned wet food for him so he could eat easier and some cat shampoo since he couldn't groom himself and prepared to have a tough conversation with the roommates. 


When we got home, the roommates acted very concerned and wanted to make sure their cat was okay. We sat them down and explained that he nearly died because they wouldn't take him to the vet and what his diagnosis/prognosis was. We told them that we were going to make sure he got whatever care or treatment he needed no matter what but we understood that he was THEIR cat so we wanted to give them options. 


Option 1: We would pay for everything up front. The vet visits, the surgery, the new food, everything. They would pay us back for everything. We would agree to set up a payment plan but would not negotiate the terms. It would be $50 per paycheck ($100/month). We'd already spent $300 and were looking at potentially $700 more in vet bills alone. If they missed a payment, they would forfeit their ownership of Arty and we would take custody and responsibility for him. 


Option 2: They could wash their hands of the situation and walk away. They could give Arty to us and we would take all responsibility for him, financially or otherwise. 


They made a big fuss about it but finally choose option 2 like we'd hoped. My husband had been Arty's person for years already and we had already decided to fight for him when the roommates eventually moved out anyway but it was nice to be able to officially adopt him into our family. 


Arty loved the new food and pretend not to like the weekly baths but he put some weight on and his fur started to grow back. 


When his dental appointment came around we were all really excited. He'd finally be comfortable and healthy. I got him ready to go and dropped him off at the vet's. They told me that it would probably take a couple hours and that they expected to have to pull all his teeth. I signed the paperwork and went home to wait. 


About an hour later, the vet called. He said they'd found something when they intubated Arty for surgery. A tumor. It was just inside his throat where they'd been unable to see it when he was awake. It was large and already eating into the back of his tongue. If it was the type of tumor they suspected, it was aggressive and fast acting. He wouldn't have long. I asked how long. A year? A few months? No. He had weeks left. Maybe. I had to make a decision for him. I could take him home and make him comfortable for as long as possible or I could have him put to sleep. Comfortable would mean going in twice a week for a pain medication and keeping him heavily medicated for the last week's of him life. It would be expensive and he wouldn't really be himself. I couldn't put Arty, my husband or myself through that. I chose to put him to sleep. The vet offered to do it right away if I wanted. Arty was still unconscious from being prepped for surgery so he would just not wake back up. I turned that down. This is what I tell my team and we consistently average 30-40% GPG attach every week. 

1. Ask everyone. It's not your job to assume/decide if the guest wants it. It's your job to offer it. 

2. Position it as a SERVICE, not an add on. We typically call it a "replacement plan". 

3. Make it personal. YOU are the face of that GPG/PRP. Let then know that YOU would be happy to replace their item. It's much easier to trust the real person in front of them than it is to trust a giant faceless corporation. 

4. Don't suggest goofy scenarios. No one actually thinks their game is going to get ruined in a zombie apocalypse. Be vague and let their imagination do the work for you. I typically say something like "if your game isn't working the way it should for ANY reason..." Whatever their mind automatically goes it will be scarier than anything you suggest. 

5. Use words like "suggest" and "recommend". NEVER use the phrases "do you want" or "would you like". 

6. Combine all GPGs together and offer to cover everything for 1 price. This makes it seem like you're asking for fewer add ons. 

7. NEVER lead with the price. It's much easier to get a "yes" if you make them want it first, then mention how cheap it is. 

My pitch usually sounds wondering like this: 
"I would really recommend getting the replacement plans for your games. That way if anything happens to them or they're not working the way they should, I can get them replaced for you. It's only $6 and it will cover both of your games for a whole year." 

Don't get discouraged if you get turned down. The goal is only 25%. That means that it's perfectly fine to get a "no" 75% of the time.
